(get_account returns products 'in no particular order'; the spec has no field for handling order. products.names is listed in this order.)

Otherwise `no_promise` with the reason of the first product (in handling order) whose note is not a paid note: `refused` or `dispute`. (The engine's default uses the first product's ending, which may be a paid note. outcome_priority would rank refused above dispute instead of using handling order.)

It is set to up:10 for the overdraft rule, 'rounded up to the next whole multiple of £10'. The card's £5 rounding cannot be expressed.)

CL-12 note codes by product type: refused after ladder NO-REF / NC-REF / NL-REF; dispute NO-DSP / NC-DSP / NL-DSP; says already paid NO-PD / NC-PD / NL-PD. (events.*.note takes a single code. The overdraft codes are used, so credit card (NC-*) and personal loan (NL-*) notes cannot be expressed.)

From 18 November 2026 (calls on that day included), the overdraft and credit card dispute codes NO-DSP and NC-DSP are retired and both are replaced by `NX-QRY`. The loan code NL-DSP does not change. (The dated change can only set one note code. NX-QRY is set, which is correct for overdraft and card but not for the loan, whose code stays NL-DSP.)

rules.opening_blocks_repeat.derivation: The opening ask is an attempt, so it is an offer already made. A step with the same amount and date repeats it.

rules.too_much_skips_full.requirement: "It's too much" counts as a refusal of the step on the table.
rules.too_much_skips_full.gap: Nothing in the format makes 'too much' refuse the current step and continue the ladder in order without also skipping later full-amount steps.

rules.too_much_floor.requirement: "It's too much" counts as a refusal of the step on the table.
rules.too_much_floor.gap: Both options (attempt_1, asked_date) offer the floor out of order. The brief only treats 'too much' as a refusal of the current step.

assumptions: Authority order: memo FL-OPS-26-11 over policy COL-POL-07 and code list CL-12, which win over the email. Memo items 1, 2 and 4 (from 30 Oct 2026) are applied, since the spec is for calls going forward.
Band A deadline is the 5th business day after today (memo item 1 replaces the 7th).
Closure days: 2026-11-13 removed and 2026-11-30 added (memo item 2). Remaining: 2026-12-24, 12-25, 12-28, 12-31 and 2027-01-01.
Overdraft floor is 20% of arrears (memo item 4), rounded up to a multiple of £10, minimum £50, capped at the arrears.

Credit card floor is 15% of arrears, rounded up to a multiple of £5 (exact multiples unchanged), minimum £30, capped at the arrears. Checks: arrears £100 → 15 → 15 → 30. Arrears £400 → 60 → 60. Arrears £20 → 3 → 5 → 30 → capped at 20.
Overdraft checks: arrears £300 → 60 → 60. Arrears £260 → 52 → 60. Arrears £100 → 20 → 20 → 50. Arrears £40 → floor £40.
floor_round and floor_min are given per product type as objects, because the card and overdraft rules differ.

Personal loan floor is the instalment in bands A and B. In band C it is the full arrears (band C floor_full_types). The instalment is capped at the arrears by the engine. The email's 'monthly instalment, full stop' is overridden by the policy.
Identity: postcode, then birth year. Two wrong answers in total end the check (policy 2.1 and API). The email's 'three goes' is overridden.
Postcode has no fixed length (UK postcodes vary), so length is omitted. It is sent in capitals with a space before the last three characters.
opening_is_attempt is true, so band attempts are the brief's totals (A 3, B 4, C 3) with the opening included, and ladder step 1 is the opening 'full today' ask.
Band A sequence: opening, full on the 2nd business day, full on the deadline. The floor step is never reached.
Band C sequence: the deadline equals the 2nd business day, so step 3 repeats step 2. It is skipped silently but still uses an attempt, and the product then ends refused.
Band B deadline rolls to the last business day of the next month when today is the last business day of the month or later (roll_if_not_after_today).
Band C upper bound is set to 99999 to stand for '61 or more'. days_overdue values outside all bands get the engine default.
Note codes are given per product type as objects, following CL-12's per-type table. Dispute codes change to NX-QRY for overdraft and credit card from 2026-11-18. NL-DSP stays.
Hardship transfers straight to the 'care' queue with no notes (policy 2.9). The hardship event is handed_over / hardship with no note.
Restructuring goes to queue 'plans' (handed_over / plans). A request for a person goes to queue 'general' (handed_over / general) without asking first, per the email.
service_error: the materials give no close reason for a system failure. no_promise / refused is used with note N-SYS.

not_reached has no reasons in the materials, but the API requires one. The reasons used are callback, no_callback, wrong_number, deceased and unclear. No reason code table is given because the materials do not list them.
Callbacks are not covered by the brief. Defaults used: today or next business day, 10:00 to 19:00, 2 asks.
max_not_talk 2, confirm.max_asks 2 and date_rules following_week are defaults; the brief says nothing about them.
The brief requires no SMS or call-recording sentence, so sms_line is empty. Changing a promise on the call is not covered, so the agent says it cannot be done on this call.
Amounts are in pounds in get_account and are multiplied by 100 to whole pence for create_promise.
The API has no hints field, so identity hints are empty.
